title: Training-Free Structured Diffusion Guidance for Compositional Text-to-Image Synthesis
role: Earliest training-free fix that blames CLIP's causal token mixing for leakage and patches the cross-attention values with per-noun-phrase encodings; a weak, cheap, box-free candidate fix
enters: a combination: text encoder (causal mask lets a later token absorb earlier tokens' meaning) and, as a second cause, cross-attention maps that spill one subject's token onto the other
enters_evidence: argument plus two single-image demonstrations: a token swap gives a red apple a green patch (Fig. 11 left), and the token 'bird' attends to a bear's mouth, which grows a beak (Fig. 11 right); p. 14 contradicts the second cause
changes: every cross-attention layer at all 50 steps: attention map from the full prompt's keys, output averaged over values from the full prompt and from each separately encoded noun phrase, O_t = (1/(k+1)) sum_i M_t V_i
training: nothing trained; needs a constituency parser (Stanza) or scene-graph parser to extract noun phrases; no boxes, masks, LLM or reference image
model: SD1.4, 50 PLMS steps, guidance 7.5; resolution not printed
similar_subjects: no similar-subject split; CC-500 pools all two-object prompts of the form 'a [colorA] [objectA] and a [colorB] [objectB]'
which_pairs: argued from token position: the later subject token carries the earlier one's meaning through CLIP's causal mask; nothing measured per pair, noun-noun text similarity not measured
when: not measured; attention maps shown from step 50 to step 1 for two prompts, with the method forming the clock region's attention earlier (Fig. 9)
cost: no extra UNet passes; k extra text encodings per prompt and k extra value products per cross-attention layer; no seconds printed here (Magnet's paper measured 7.94 s against 6.62 s for SD1.4, +20.0%)
headline: CC-500 human labels on SD1.4: both objects present in 38.0% of images against 34.5% for plain SD; both in the right colours 22.7% against 19.2%
suggests: (inferred) a box-free, zero-extra-pass fix that CO3 could host using its two subject names as noun phrases, but its measured gain is small and Magnet's human study rates it close to plain SD

quotes.text: Our key observation is that the contextualization of CLIP embeddings is a potential cause of incorrect attribute binding.
Due to the causal attention masks, tokens in the later part of a sequence are blended with the token semantics before them.
Thus, the inaccurate attention maps lead to a beak-like mouth of the bear in the image.
This result proves that the token “red” is contaminated with the semantics of “green” before it
This proves that inaccurate attention distributions contribute little to the final image content.
By modifying the key-value pairs in cross-attention layers, we manage to map the encoding of each text span into attended regions in 2D image space.
We use W p to obtain Kp and M t as in Eq. 1, assuming that the full-prompt key is able to generate layouts without missing objects.
